text.p: Headlines from major national newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
EL PAIS
- Police investigates possible kidnapping by Basque separatists of son of Basque businessman.
- Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar proposes to European Union plan of economic sanctions against Cuba.
- Four Spanish priests killed in Zaire were thrown into pit by Hutu militia.
EL MUNDO
- Police fear Delclaux son has been kidnapped by ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom).
- Socialists offer parliamentary support to ruling conservative Popular Party (PP) if it breaks with nationalists.

- Witness says Civil Guard General Enrique Rodriguez Galindo, suspect in kidnapping, torture and murder of two presumed Basque separatists in 1980s "dirty war" against ETA, has accounts in Miami and Panama.
DIARIO 16
- Possible kidnapping of son of important Basque businessman.
- PP criticises Socialists for asking for pensions for housewives.
ABC
- Legion prepares to be sent to Zaire on humanitarian mission.
CINCO DIAS
- Government reforms work contracts.
- Merger between Axa and UAP creates world's second largest insurer.
- Company boards trying to gain more control over executives.
EXPANSION
- Economy Minister Rodrigo Rato authorises 34 billion peseta credit to state broadcaster RTVE to last until year-end.
- Government plans to cut pensions if inflation grows by less than expected.
- Fund buying propels bourse to new high.
- Lowering electricity tariff will save 600 billion pesetas.
GACETA DE LOS NEGOCIOS
- Iberia privatisation takes off with search for partner.
- European Union members obtained 5.6 percent of total budget through fraud in 1995.
- Employment Minister Javier Arenas admits reforming pensions needs business support.
- Paolo Gallone, trustee of disgraced former Banesto chairman Mario Conde, says Conde hid fortune in Switzerland.
